made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/mostrador-sheet-make.js, from mostrador-set.html (window.MOSTRADOR.CD, CF) and the design of El mostrador (version 2, with the calle state, and the orchestrator's pass 3). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX, OY = H / 2 + originY. A box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the floor; z 1: the counter top; z .45: the seat) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty: the lowest drawn row is 54), 46 sitting (a 49-row canvas); the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (so row 25 of the canvas is on sy, as juego.js frogBox: his shadow line q.y + 25); abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30, drawn rows 0 to 49; abuela sitting mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17 (her middle) and row 36 (her lap) on (sx, sy), the spot being the seat; a small thing: its bottom middle on the point
rules.view: a view has a zoom (here 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture) and x0 = clamp(round(sx - 98), 0, 44), sx the projection of its world point. Never a fraction
rules.person: for the check "seen from the thighs up": a person is 53 rows tall (the standing figure's drawn rows), at least 28 of them above the counter's top back edge at his column
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character
rules.clear: a spot keeps 4 px from the pixels the set draws for the register (part caja), the freezer (part nevera, nevera = 1) and the chair (part silla): the distance from the spot's feet pixel (column sx, row sy - 1) to the nearest such pixel. A spot of the design that was nearer moved along x by the least step of .01 that clears it: spots[name].moved says from where

dentro.what: inside the shop: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture, centred on this point (x0 = clamp(round(sx - 98), 0, 44)); donde=calle has its own picture and view (calle.views.calle)

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3), so the counter hides don Pepe's legs and nothing behind him hides him.
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The upright plane through the feet, as El balcón's front; the same test for people, things on the counter and goods on the shelves
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, 0, radius) at the world x, y of the spot, for a character standing on the floor (z 0)
shadows.onCounter: the frog on the counter top (z 1) casts none: the counter top is not ground in colmado-dentro.js (no slab), so a shadow has nothing to land on, and one cast at the floor under him would show in front of the counter

calle.what: the state donde=calle: the shop front from the street (colmado-fuera.js, drawn by mostrador-set.html?donde=calle); its own origin, picture and view. The depth rule, the anchors and the shadows are the same as inside (the top level of this sheet)
